verdicts.quote: “This authentication method is for developers building integrations with Grain to be used by any Grain users. The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow…”
verdicts.reason: Docs clearly describe a standard OAuth2 flow intended for third‑party integrations. ([developers.grain.com](https://developers.grain.com/authentication.html))

verdicts.quote: “The ‘workspace’ scope is only available to clients verified by Grain.”
verdicts.reason: While PATs are self‑serve, production‑grade workspace access/scopes require Grain verification, which fits “app_review” rather than “self_serve_free.” ([developers.grain.com](https://developers.grain.com/authentication.html))

verdicts.quote: “retrieve recordings, transcripts, AI notes and action items, participants, tags, teams, and meeting types… Manage recordings… Receive real‑time events…”
verdicts.reason: Vendor docs show many resource types and actions (recordings, users/teams, playlists, uploads, stories, hooks), consistent with a broad API. ([support.grain.com](https://support.grain.com/en/articles/15507288-grain-api?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “Grain’s official MCP server is available now for all users!”
verdicts.reason: Grain publishes and maintains an official MCP server and quick‑start guide. ([grain.com](https://grain.com/release-notes?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: “The ‘workspace’ scope is only available to clients verified by Grain.”
verdicts.reason: Creds and docs are self‑serve for personal scope, but lack of sandbox and review/plan gating for workspace scope are practical caveats. ([developers.grain.com](https://developers.grain.com/authentication.html))
